title: Book Three · Chapter 48: Four at the Park
story:
On Sunday morning, Kai waits at the park with his ball.

His friend is there too. Ronan brings Leo along the path. Before they reach the bench, the ball rolls toward their feet.

Leo stops it with his shoe.

“Kai?” he asks.

“Leo?”

“The feet arrived.”

Kai grins. “I can see.”

Ronan introduces the other boy. Then Kai takes the ball to a clear patch of grass.

There are no goal posts. They put two bags at one end and two coats at the other.

Leo looks at Ronan.

“Us two?”

Ronan starts to nod. Kai's friend has already moved beside him. They played together all week before the holiday.

For a moment, four boys stand still.

“We can change after a while,” Kai says.

Leo nods and goes to his side. Ronan feels a small tightness in his chest. Before the game, he pictured himself beside Leo. He did not think about the other boys.

Then the ball comes toward him. He sends it to Kai's friend and runs ahead.

Leo is quicker than Ronan remembers. He reaches the next pass first and turns toward the bags.

“New bus practice?” Ronan calls.

“I can't miss the doors.”

His shot goes past one bag. Kai runs after it and brings it back.

They play until their shirts feel hot. Then they sit beneath a tree with their bottles.

Kai asks about the other city. Leo tells him about a sports shop with a whole wall of balls.

“All different?”

“Some just different colours.”

“That is still a lot of balls.”

Ronan takes a drink. Kai and Leo are already talking over each other. He feels pleased, then strangely quiet.

Leo turns to him.

“You pass better now.”

“I practise.”

“With these two?”

Ronan nods.

“Usually at school.”

Leo picks a dry piece of grass from his shoe. “Good.”

Kai stands up. He wants another game. This time, Ronan and Leo play on the same side.

The first pass goes wrong. Ronan runs left while Leo sends the ball right.

“I moved,” Ronan says.

“I noticed.”

They laugh. On the next turn, Leo looks before he passes. Ronan calls before he runs.

Kai still stops their shot. He lifts both hands and grins.

“Visitors don't get free goals.”

At noon, Leo needs to return to his grandmother's for lunch.

The four boys walk to the park entrance. Tomorrow, Anna has time to meet Ronan and Leo at the hall in the afternoon.

Leo takes the ball once more from Kai's hand, then gives it back.

“A good ball,” he says.

“A bad name,” Ronan answers.

Kai looks at both of them. “You told him?”

Ronan laughs. Kai and his friend turn toward another street to meet someone. Ronan and Leo part from them at the gate.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

goal post＝球门柱；chest＝胸口；visitor＝来访的人；part＝分开、分别（本章作动词）。

## 理解问题

1. 第一轮分队为什么让Ronan和Leo有一瞬间的尴尬？
2. 换回旧搭档后，他们是不是立刻配合无误？后来怎样调整？

## 读句子

**This time, Ronan and Leo play on the same side.**

拆开看：This time, / Ronan and Leo / play on the same side.

这一次／Ronan和Leo／在同一队踢球。
